clue.text: Force in a number of Germans is nothing to joke about

parts.note: to force someone to do something is to make them do it

indicators.note: the zero is placed in the middle of the German numeral, which surrounds it

parts.note: a German number: funf (fünf) is German for five
nothing is zero, the round letter O

explanation.surface: Some sort of German military force seems to be no laughing matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A number of Germans' is not a crowd but a numeral in German, five; 'in' puts the zero inside that numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic phrase: to tease or ridicule someone is to joke about them.

clue.text: In jet fighter, up goes British chief

indicators.note: the British letters go into the fighter's name

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian jet fighter

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read upwards, i.e. backwards

explanation.surface: A British air commander climbs into a captured enemy jet.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a crime boss or ringleader, the top man behind an operation.

clue.text: After fun with prostitute one has to get going

indicators.note: the fun word comes first, with the prostitute word after it

parts.note: doing it for kicks means for fun
tart is slang for a prostitute

explanation.surface: After a fling with a prostitute, a man must hurry on his way.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to give something a vigorous start, as a motorbike started by a kick on its pedal.

clue.text: Since end of April, nothing but overwhelming resistance, sadly

parts.note: for can mean since, because

indicators.note: the last letter of April is taken
the word for nothing but overwhelms the resistance letter, engulfing it

parts.note: only means nothing but, merely
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Since late April a campaign has met only crushing opposition, to everyone's regret.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: done in a hopeless, pitiful way, so miserably or forlorn-seeming.

clue.text: Dope on bed — bloke nabbed by fat detectives

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above, i.e. before

parts.note: dope is slang for information, the news
a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: the bloke is grabbed and held inside the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
Andy is any ordinary bloke's name

explanation.surface: Drugs found on a bed, and a fat cop nabs a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonym: headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police, standing for its detectives as a whole.

clue.text: Aussie spinner making sport quietly bewilders opening pair of English bats

parts.note: fun is sport, as in making sport of someone

indicators.note: bats, i.e. crazy, signals the letters are mixed up

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quietly
the first two letters of English

explanation.surface: An Australian spin bowler baffles England's two opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' and 'bats' look like cricket, but the spinner spins webs, and 'bats' (mad) means rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous Australian spider that spins a funnel-shaped web; spinner is a fair description of any web-maker.

clue.text: Having rearranged The King and I, sends up Dickensian villain

indicators.note: the musical's title signals that the king's letter and the I swap places in the word

parts.note: to sky a ball is to send it high up, so sends up = skies
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone reworking the musical The King and I and lampooning it in the process.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The King and I' is not the show: it means the K and the I of SKIES change places, giving S-I-K-E-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes is the brutal housebreaker in Dickens's novel Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Sharpen up sportsman's displays

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters read upwards, backwards
the word sportsman's displays some of its own letters, shown inside it

explanation.surface: An athlete shows off how he hones his edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is a leather strap for honing razors, and to strop a blade is to sharpen it.

clue.text: Put out cold meat in salad for leaf-eater

parts.note: to knock out cold is KO, the boxing abbreviation

indicators.note: the meat, the inside, of the word salad, i.e. its middle letters

explanation.surface: Leave cold meat out of the salad to suit a vegetarian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold meat' looks like one food item, but 'Put out cold' is KO and 'meat in' takes the middle of salad.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial lives on eucalyptus leaves alone, so it is a leaf-eater.

clue.text: Less sound old lifeboat with mostly poor material

indicators.note: the pieces are joined together, one with the next

parts.note: sh is a request for quiet, for less sound
Noah's ark, the original lifeboat

indicators.note: most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for penniless

explanation.surface: A quieter old lifeboat made largely of shoddy fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A fabric: a smooth stiff cloth of rayon or wool, or leather made from shark hide.

clue.text: Second serious disagreement for Twickenham trio

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a row is a heated quarrel

explanation.surface: Seconding a motion at the rugby club leads to a big argument.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home stadium of English rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the back row is the trio of forwards at the rear of the scrum: two flankers and the number eight.

clue.text: State finally acquired Irish verse covered by old lady of pop

indicators.note: the grandmother word wraps round the Irish and verse letters, covering them

parts.note: nana is a grandmother, mother of one's pop (father)

explanation.surface: A grandmother of the pop charts records a cover of an Irish song.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is three words long: the Buddhist goal is the state one finally acquires.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the ultimate state of enlightenment, reached at last after the cycle of rebirth.

clue.text: Get up suddenly with old enthusiasm

parts.note: wind that gets up suddenly is a gust

explanation.surface: Someone leaping up with their former eagerness.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: zest and relish in doing something, keen enjoyment.

clue.text: Poor vet lands a parking fine in Hanover

indicators.note: the check word lands, i.e. catches, the other pieces inside it as a fisherman lands a fish

parts.note: to vet something is to check it
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
ja is German for yes, i.e. fine, all right

explanation.surface: A vet receives a parking ticket while in the German city of Hanover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' is not a penalty but German for 'yes, OK'; Hanover signals the language. 'Lands' means the vetting word catches the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, cheapjack means shoddy and inferior, i.e. of poor quality.

clue.text: Odds and ends of exotica, new and uncommon produce

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at a race's start

indicators.note: the final letters of the three words that follow are taken

explanation.surface: A strange new range of exotic produce on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds and ends' looks like a single phrase, but 'Odds' gives SP and 'ends of' picks the last letters of exotica, new and uncommon: A, W, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: fish and frogs lay eggs, i.e. produce young, in great numbers.

clue.text: Section of kitchen associated with alcoholic drinks

parts.note: sided with means took the part of, aligned with
rums are glasses of spirit

explanation.surface: Part of a kitchen given over to the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kitchen' is orchestral slang for the percussion section, not a room for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Snare drums are part of the orchestra's percussion, nicknamed the kitchen, so they form a section of it.

clue.text: Citizens draw in County Men's Society

parts.note: to draw a cart is to tow it

indicators.note: within the county's name, the men are changed to society, one swapped for the other

parts.note: Norfolk is an English county in East Anglia
OR (other ranks) is the crossword abbreviation for soldiers or men; the 's reads as 'is', i.e. becomes

explanation.surface: Residents attracting people into a county gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'in County, Men is Society': within the county name the soldiers' abbreviation gives way to the society letter. Norfolk is a county in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: the people who live in a town, its inhabitants or residents.

clue.text: Lasting impression left —- it cheers up composer

parts.note: a scar is a mark left for good

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the two pieces read upwards, backwards

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A lasting mark on the left of a toast that cheers a composer up.
explanation.definitionFit: Domenico (or Alessandro) Scarlatti, Italian Baroque composers, famed for keyboard sonatas.

clue.text: Like birds, often not for cooking and carving

definitions.meaning: flying, in flight, as birds often are
a bird still flying is not yet on the table for roasting and slicing

explanation.surface: Birds in flight are not ready for the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading plays on a wing being a joint to carve; a bird in the air is nobody's dinner yet.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: flying, in flight, as birds are when airborne rather than settled.

clue.text: Mark birthday with stirring old hymn

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up, mixed into a new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for the old German currency, the mark

explanation.surface: Celebrating someone's birthday with a rousing traditional song.
explanation.definitionFit: A choral song of ancient Greece in honour of Dionysus, so a very old hymn; later any wild, ecstatic verse.

clue.text: Chekhov's wife leaving without provocation

definitions.note: possessive, meaning the first name belonging to the Russian writer

indicators.note: the wife's letter departs from the word, leaving the rest

parts.note: gratuitous, unprovoked, as in an unprovoked attack

explanation.surface: The playwright's wife walks out on him for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chekhov's wife' looks like the definition, but the wife is W; 'Chekhov's' alone defines, as Chekhov's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian dramatist's given name, so this is Chekhov's: Anton Pavlovich Chekhov.

clue.text: In America, maybe moonlight swim after large drink?

indicators.note: the swim word comes after the drink word

parts.note: a double is a twice-sized measure of spirits
a dip is a quick swim

explanation.surface: A late-night swim after a big drink, American style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moonlight swim' looks like a single picture; 'moonlight' is the verb meaning to hold a second job.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang: to draw two incomes, e.g. a pension plus a salary, much as moonlighting means working a second job.

clue.text: Turnips, even bits kept for one, no longer freeze

indicators.note: the even-numbered letters, second, fourth and sixth, are taken

parts.note: EG, for example, means for one

explanation.surface: Turnip scraps kept for someone, no longer to be frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: To unpeg prices or wages is to release them from a fixed level, so they are no longer held still.

clue.text: Bounded where ends of line meet

indicators.note: the first and last letters of the word line

parts.note: meet is an old word for fitting, suitable

explanation.surface: A boundary marking the point where two lines meet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' is the archaic adjective meaning proper, as in 'it is meet and right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of leap, so jumped or sprang, as bounded means here.

clue.text: It drains one after skirt's caught tip of spike

indicators.note: the womaniser word catches the tip letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a lech (lecher) chases after skirt, i.e. women

indicators.note: the tip here is the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Something snagged on a spike drains away someone's skirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodsucking worm drains blood from its host; figuratively a parasite drains others' resources.

clue.text: Silent star's leg severed by weapon

indicators.note: the leg is cut away, severed from the weapon

parts.note: a harpoon is a whaling weapon
on is leg, the cricket term for the leg side of the field

explanation.surface: A film star's leg is cut off by a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so leg = ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Marx Brother who never spoke on screen, communicating by mime and his horn.

clue.text: Increased pressure unfortunately set back Swedish town

parts.note: prices that have gone up have increased
P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics

indicators.note: the word for unfortunately is set back, i.e. written backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning unfortunately

explanation.surface: Rising pressure has been a setback for a town in Sweden.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swedish city north of Stockholm, home to Scandinavia's oldest university.

clue.text: Point bank makes with even less reason

parts.note: a dot is a point
a tier is a bank, e.g. of seats or oars

explanation.surface: A banker's pointed remark about what makes the bank's money.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of dotty, crazy: dottier means sillier, showing still less sense.

clue.text: Picked up quote giving a good deal

indicators.note: picked up by ear, as a radio picks up a signal, so the word is heard

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: Someone picks up on a quotation that offers a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal' is not a bargain but 'much', as in 'a sight better'.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adverb: 'a sight better' means considerably better, by a great amount.

clue.text: Being out after dark, at first cook displays evidence of bravery

indicators.note: the straying word follows the first letter of dark
only the opening letter of dark is used

parts.note: erring is being out, i.e. wrong, off target
to do food is to cook it, as in done to a turn

explanation.surface: Out late after dark, a chef starts showing signs of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: An old phrase for heroic daring and feats of courage, so it is shown as evidence of bravery.
